skill.name: snowtower-admin
skill.description: Guide SnowTower administrators through SnowDDL deployments, Snowflake user provisioning, role grants, CI/CD operations, troubleshooting, and security checks.
skill.summary: Administer SnowTower Snowflake infrastructure with guided SnowDDL, user, role, deployment, and security workflows.
skill.author: Database-Tycoon

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown documentation or legitimate administrative command examples, not hidden code execution. Confirmed risks remain because the skill guides privileged Snowflake operations, references private keys and .env secrets, updates GitHub secrets, and documents an emergency account exception without network policy.

remediation.issue: Sensitive Snowflake private key and Fernet key handling is documented in local files and environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to paste secret values into AI tools, require approved secret storage, and prefer short-lived or managed credentials where possible.

remediation.issue: Emergency recovery account is documented without network policy and with password authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Add compensating controls such as strong MFA, break-glass approval, audit logging, credential rotation, and periodic access review.

remediation.issue: Many workflows require ACCOUNTADMIN or equivalent high-privilege Snowflake access.
remediation.suggestion: Encourage least-privilege roles for routine tasks and reserve ACCOUNTADMIN for narrowly scoped deployment or recovery procedures.

remediation.issue: The guide includes commands that can modify Snowflake infrastructure, GitHub secrets, and repository state.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation steps before destructive or shared-state commands, especially deploy, rollback, key reset, and push operations.

content.value_statement: Snowflake infrastructure changes can be risky when users, roles, schemas, and deployments are managed manually. This skill gives SnowTower administrators structured workflows for SnowDDL planning, safe deployment, provisioning, troubleshooting, and security checks.
actual_capabilities: Provides a SnowDDL deployment workflow that previews changes before applying them.
Explains Snowflake user creation through an interactive wizard, YAML edits, or command-line flags.
Documents role hierarchy, business roles, technical roles, and grants used by SnowTower.
Guides database, schema, warehouse, and network policy configuration through YAML examples.
Lists CI/CD, troubleshooting, rollback, service account reset, health check, and audit commands.
Highlights security operations for MFA checks, network policies, and emergency access documentation.
limitations: Requires an existing SnowTower repository with the referenced scripts and SnowDDL layout.
Assumes the operator has authorized Snowflake, GitHub, and local shell access.
Does not verify production safety unless the operator reviews plans and command output.
Includes privileged administration workflows that should not be used by untrusted users.

use_cases.title: Deploy SnowDDL changes safely
use_cases.description: Preview SnowDDL changes, inspect grants and drops, then apply changes through the safer deployment wrapper.

use_cases.title: Provision Snowflake users and roles
use_cases.description: Create users, assign business roles, configure authentication, and understand role inheritance in SnowTower.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot production administration issues
use_cases.description: Diagnose authentication failures, schema grant drift, locked users, warehouse status, and service account resets.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me preview my SnowTower SnowDDL changes and explain which plan output lines need careful review before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Add a new Snowflake user
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through adding a new Snowflake user in SnowTower with the right user type, default role, warehouse, and authentication fields.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate schema grant drift
prompt_templates.prompt: The SnowDDL plan shows many schema grant revokes. Help me determine whether this is drift and how to deploy safely.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an emergency account reset
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cautious step-by-step plan to reset the SnowTower Snowflake service account keys and update dependent GitHub secrets.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy SnowDDL changes.
output_examples.output: A cautious deployment checklist: preview the plan, review create, alter, drop, grant, and revoke statements, confirm admin role changes, then apply through the safe deployment workflow.
A troubleshooting path that checks authentication configuration, user status, MFA registration, login history, and whether an administrator must unlock the account.

output_examples.input: We need to add a new analyst role.
output_examples.output: A role design summary that separates user assignment, business role membership, technical role grants, warehouse access, and schema read permissions.

best_practices: Run a plan command and review destructive changes before every deployment.
Limit use of administrator roles and document emergency access activity.
Store private keys and encryption keys in approved secret management systems.
anti_patterns: Do not apply SnowDDL changes without reviewing drops, revokes, and admin role changes.
Do not paste private keys, Fernet keys, or Snowflake credentials into chat prompts.
Do not use emergency accounts for routine operations or convenience access.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for authorized SnowTower infrastructure, security, DevOps, and on-call administrators.

faq.question: Does it make changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples. Operators still approve and run commands in their environment.

faq.question: Why does it emphasize deployment previews?
faq.answer: SnowDDL plans can include drops, revokes, and admin role changes. Reviewing the plan reduces production change risk.

faq.question: Can it help with user onboarding?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains interactive, YAML, and command-line flows for creating Snowflake users and assigning roles.

faq.question: What secrets are involved?
faq.answer: The guide references Snowflake private keys, Fernet keys, environment files, and GitHub secrets for authorized administration.

faq.question: Is it safe for general marketplace auto-install?
faq.answer: It should be treated as privileged administration content because it references ACCOUNTADMIN, secrets, and emergency access procedures.
